No, that is not true. According to Swiss law, the general requirement for naturalization is a minimum of 10 years of legal residence in Switzerland, including at least three years in the five years immediately preceding the application. However, this is the federal minimum requirement. The actual process and requirements can be stricter at the cantonal and municipal levels, where additional criteria related to integration, language skills, and knowledge of Swiss society and politics are assessed.

Additionally, the type of residence permit (such as a B permit) does not reduce the required duration of residence for naturalization. The 10-year federal requirement applies regardless of the permit type, though the specific integration requirements may vary by canton.
